literal_contracts.Definition:
Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by
$$P_A:=\sum_B d_{A,B}(s)\,M_B,\qquad\text{so that}\qquad M_A=\sum_B p_{A,B}(-s)\,P_B .$$
The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

The **reverse-factor monomials** $\widetilde M_A$ use the reverse-column
reading of the tableau $A$; the corresponding bar-fixed families
$\widetilde L_A,\widetilde T_A$ are defined by the same triangular conditions
with respect to $\widetilde M_A$, so that $\widetilde L_A$ is supported on
$B>A$. **Rectification** is the weight-preserving combinatorial identification
of the original lower ground component $\mathrm{Rev}^\Lambda$ with the
reverse-factor lower ground component $\mathrm{Std}^\Lambda$, given by reading
down columns and reverse row insertion.

The **source sesquilinear form** is the $\mathbb C$-antilinear-in-the-first
argument pairing with
$$\langle M_A,\psi M_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},$$
and the **bilinear reverse-factor form** is
$$C(\widetilde M_A,\psi M_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$
Thus the labelled monomial Gram matrices of the two forms are the inverse
ordinary-bar matrix, not the identity. Transition duality gives
$$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$

All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and
commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings. On a highest
constituent, the source bilinear normalization $C_0$ and the library
polarization of [[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]] differ by
an explicit weight power, proved in the global-basis comparison later in this
pair; no unqualified library-upper/ordinary-bar identification is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and that $I$ is bounded
below, so $n_j=m_j+1-\inf(I)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are finite; the upper end of
$I$ may remain unbounded. Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let
the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi
$\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).
For a tableau $A$ with column reading $a_1,\dots,a_n$ (read column by column,
bottom to top, [[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]]) put
$$\lambda_A=\sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_j+j-1)\,\varepsilon_j .$$
Strict columns make $\lambda_A$ Levi-dominant, so that the simple highest weight
module $L(A)$ of [[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]]
and the induced generalized standard
$M(A)=M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda_A)$ of
[[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]] belong to the genuine
parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]].

Use the published **half-sum convention**
$\rho_j=(n+1-2j)/2$; then
$$\lambda_{A,j}+\rho_j=a_j+\frac{n-1}{2},$$
so the $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ Harish-Chandra shifted-coordinate multiset of the
block is the tableau-entry multiset plus the common scalar $(n-1)/2$, and this
multiset together with the displayed scalar $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ centre labels the
central character ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). The Fock
weight $\sum_j\delta_{a_j}=\Lambda-\alpha$ of the Fock item belongs to the
different $\mathfrak{gl}_{I^+}$ weight lattice and indexes that entry multiset;
it is **not** a literal $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ highest weight.

For an entry multiset $\alpha$ the corresponding **finite parabolic central
block** $\mathcal O^\Lambda_\alpha$ has labels
$\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda_\alpha$, generalized standards $M(A)$, simples $L(A)$,
projective covers $P(A)$ and costandards $\nabla(A)$, with the BGG reciprocity,
restricted duality and highest-weight structure inherited from
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]; by
[[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]] it is a single
linkage block. Its simple and standard classes form bases of its Grothendieck
group, and its numerical multiplicities include repeated-entry singular central
characters. The direct sum over the admitted entry multisets is
$\mathcal O^\Lambda$. **Opposite blocks** use the reversed Levi order and the
reverse-column reading, with the correspondingly reversed label order
([[lem-the-parabolic-semi-regular-duality-and-reverse-column-label-map]]).

Keep the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, and the truncated tensor space
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. The **stable
range** for $\lambda$ is the condition
$$q_l\ge d:$$
at least $d$ Jordan strings have the maximum length $l=p_n$, equivalently the
smallest column has height at least $d$.

The verification below records the structure attached to the stable range and
to its failure. In the stable range the raw $H_d(\mathbf a)$ action is
faithful. For admissible $c$ outside the stable range, the image of the Hecke
action is a central block corner
$$fH_d(\mathbf a)f,$$
where $f$ is the sum of the central blocks supporting the contractible simple
labels: one enlarges the pyramid by adding $r$ columns and enlarging every
$q_j$ by $r$ while preserving every root $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$, lets $e$ be the
idempotent selecting the added ground rows, identifies the supported blocks,
and deletes the added rows. The generalized-eigenvalue idempotents $e(\mathbf i)$
are not individually central; $f$ is a sum of entire central blocks, so the
corner is a two-sided algebraic object. For nonadmissible $c$ the genuine
image algebra and the full tensor double centralizer still exist by
[[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]],
but the same central-corner/Morita conclusion is not inferred without
admissibility.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as inherited from the
category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers below. Fix a finite genuine parabolic central
summand: an integral block $\mathcal C$ of a parabolic category
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ ([[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]])
that is a **finite highest-weight block** with the following data.

(1) A finite label set $\Lambda$ with a partial order $\preceq$ (in the
parabolic/finite-type-$A$ setting this is the tableau order on the labels of
the block, i.e. the dominance order on the relevant highest weights); for each
$A\in\Lambda$ a standard object $\Delta_A$ and a costandard object $\nabla_A$
of $\mathcal C$, with
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(\Delta_A,\nabla_B)=\begin{cases}\mathbb C,&A=B,\\ 0,&A\neq B,\end{cases}\qquad \operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal C}(\Delta_A,\nabla_B)=0\ \ (j\ge 1).$$

(2) The block is basic with finite-dimensional homomorphism spaces, every
object has finite length, and for each $A$ the projective cover $P_A$ of the
simple head $L_A$ of $\Delta_A$, respectively the injective envelope
$I_A=\nabla_A$ of the simple socle $L_A$ of $\nabla_A$, has a finite
$\Delta$-flag, respectively a finite $\nabla$-flag, with multiplicities
$$(P_A:\Delta_B)=(\nabla_B:L_A)=[\Delta_B:L_A]$$
(BGG reciprocity).

A **finite standard flag** ($\Delta$-flag) of $N\in\mathcal C$ is a finite
chain $0=N_0\subseteq N_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq N_n=N$ of subobjects with
$N_i/N_{i-1}\cong\Delta_{A_i}$ for all $i$; a **finite costandard flag**
($\nabla$-flag) is defined verbatim with $\nabla_{A_i}$. Write
$\mathcal F(\Delta)$, respectively $\mathcal F(\nabla)$, for the full
subcategory of objects of $\mathcal C$ admitting such a flag (the zero object
has the empty flag). For $N\in\mathcal F(\Delta)$ and $A\in\Lambda$ the
**multiplicity** $(N:\Delta_A)$ is the number of indices $i$ with $A_i=A$;
this number is independent of the chosen flag by step 2.2 below. A **tilting
object** is an object lying in $\mathcal F(\Delta)\cap\mathcal F(\nabla)$.

An indecomposable tilting object with $\Delta$-flag having $\Delta_A$ exactly
once, as its lowest factor, and all remaining factors $\Delta_B$ with
$B\prec A$, is **normalized at** $A$ and written $T_A$; existence is supplied
by the classification theorem proved later in this pair, and by step 2.1 any
such object is the unique indecomposable tilting object with $A$ as its unique
maximal support label, by step 2.1. In a lower ideal $\Gamma\subseteq\Lambda$ (i.e.
$B\preceq A\in\Gamma$ implies $B\in\Gamma$) containing $A$, the object $T_A$
is a summand of the tilting generator of the Serre subcategory determined by
$\Gamma$ and is unchanged by the passage to $\Gamma$ (step 3.1).

Keep the pyramid and admissible origins $c$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], the
ground object $P_c$, the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ and its
central decomposition. For a charge $\alpha\in Q^+$ with $\mathrm{ht}(\alpha)=d$
let $I_\alpha$ be the finite set of residue sequences of content $\alpha$, and
let $T_\alpha$ be the corresponding central component of $T$; in the integral
model
$$T_\alpha=\sum_{i\in I_\alpha}f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}P_c,$$
the sum of the residue-induction images of the ground object. Put
$$B_\alpha:=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}},$$
the corresponding central component of the Hecke image algebra (the opposite
convention is fixed here), and define the **Schur functor** of the block by
$$\pi_\alpha:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha,-)\colon\mathcal O_\alpha^d\to B_\alpha\text{-mod}.$$
Its left adjoint is $\pi^*_\alpha:=T_\alpha\otimes_{B_\alpha}-$.

The verification below records the properties used on this page and marks the
boundaries explicitly: $\pi_\alpha$ is exact, being Hom from a projective
object; its left adjoint is right exact but not exact in general; it sends
$B_\alpha$-projectives to projective objects and $\pi^*_\alpha\pi_\alpha$
recovers $\operatorname{add}(T_\alpha)$, including every standard-labelled
prinjective; neither exactness of $\pi^*_\alpha$ nor recovery of every
category-$\mathcal O$ projective is asserted, both failing in the two-equal-charge
rank-one example of the companion page. The components assemble as a locally
unital sum over the charges, and all ambient labels, including those killed by
$\pi$, remain in the category $\mathcal O$.

literal_contracts.Statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, a degree $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space with its finite W-algebra image
$W_d$ and cyclotomic Hecke image $B_d$. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$; this is the raw double centralizer.
2. For admissible origins, $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence between
   $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.
3. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact
   Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully
   faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all
   tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers
   $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but not every projective.
4. In the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the algebra $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic
   algebra $H_d(\mathbf a)$; outside the stable range and for admissible
   origins the central-corner identification $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ is used.

Mutual centralizers alone do not give the Morita statement: the nonadmissible
origin example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$ and $d=2$ has a nonprojective tensor
module while the mutual centralizer identities still hold.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c$ be an admissible origin, let $P_c$ be the ground
simple projective-injective of the relevant summand of the parabolic category
$\mathcal O$ of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]],
and let $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ with $V=\mathbb C^N$. Write
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ for the image of the right cyclotomic Hecke action of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] and $B_\alpha$ for its central
components. Then the right Hecke action gives an algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d,$$
and on each central component, cut by the central idempotents $f_\alpha$ of
$B_d$ acting on $T=\bigoplus_\alpha T_\alpha$,
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha =f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha,$$
where $H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$ is the corresponding block of the cyclotomic Hecke
algebra. In the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the image is the full cyclotomic
algebra, $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ and $B_\alpha=H_\alpha(\mathbf a)$; a single
component is not identified with the entire degree-$d$ algebra. Outside the
stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin
corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The maps $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ are surjective in all cases,
and the full action $H_d(\mathbf a)\to\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ is
injective precisely in the stable range.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every label $A$ in a
genuine tableau parabolic block of
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins
with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.
Equivalently, $T(A)$ has that maximal-label normalized standard flag and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1(M(B),T(A))=0$ for all $B$. Every tilting object is a finite
direct sum of these, and their classes form a unitriangular Grothendieck basis.
Restricted duality fixes $T(A)$. For a finite lower ideal $\Gamma$ containing
$A$ the corresponding partial tilting is the same ambient $T(A)$, since all
support labels are $\le A$; compatible ideal systems therefore stabilize in each
finite block, with flag-preserving inclusions. No uniqueness is claimed from a
bottom-standard occurrence alone without indecomposability and maximal support.
In the inline prinjectivity claim, $P(A)$ is projective-injective (equivalently
self-dual) exactly when $A$ is standard; in that case $P(A)=T(A^{\uparrow})$
with the proved rectification label.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the genuine tableau
$K_0$/Fock identification at $s=1$
([[thm-the-parabolic-o-grothendieck-group-is-the-integral-fock-module]]). For
every label $A$,
$$[L(A)]=L_A,\qquad [P(A)]=P_A,\qquad [T(A)]=T_A .$$
The projective coefficients are $d_{A,B}(1)$ by BGG reciprocity; the tilting
coefficients are the **opposite/reverse-column** composition coefficients
$\widetilde d_{A,B}(1)$, by the exact parabolic Ringel equivalence. They are not
generally the inverse-transpose of the original composition matrix. Simples,
projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and
canonical Fock families respectively. These are ungraded specializations; no
Koszul grading and no identification of the library upper and lower families is
asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]]. Let
$W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the
image of the finite W-algebra and let
$B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$ and every $d$, and their associated graded image
   algebras are the corresponding images of $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ and of the
   truncated polynomial/permutation algebra.
2. If $q_l\ge d$, then the action of the full cyclotomic algebra
   $H_d(\mathbf a)$ is faithful.
3. If $c$ is admissible (that is, $c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$),
   then the tensor module is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence
   between $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.

Mutual centralizers alone do not imply Morita for arbitrary $c$: the explicit
example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ on the companion page has a
nonprojective tensor module.

For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of
[[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact
on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and
$$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$
is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Both $V$ and the
Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ are fully faithful on
all projective objects of the relevant summand, and the quotient is also fully
faithful on tiltings. $T$ is a self-dual prinjective detecting object
containing all standard-labelled projective-injective covers, but it is not a
generator of the entire category-$\mathcal O$ summand. $V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$
is a projective generator of $W_d$-mod, and $V$ preserves projectivity on
$\operatorname{add}(T)$; it need not send every projective of $\mathcal O$ to
a projective $W$-module. The composite of $V$ with the Morita equivalence is
the Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples.

proposed_exact_proof_derivations.claim: The Specht isomorphism. Choose a sufficiently large admissible stable realization in which the pyramid has $d$ distinct full ground rows; the row-torus weight idempotent $e_S$ of those rows is an element of the finite-W image, commuting with the Hecke action, and $e_SV_c^{\otimes d}$ has dimension $l^dd!$ with the words using the $d$ chosen rows as a basis, so evaluation at the regular vector identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ with $e_S(-)$. The corner operators are the row permutations together with $h(x_i)=e_S(-D^{(2)}_{r_i}+e_2(c)+e_1(c)+d-n-i+1)e_S$, where $D^{(2)}_{r_i}$ is the degree-two Gauss/path coefficient; on the canonical colour fibre of the finite Levi standard $V(A)$ this acts by $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ plus the within-column Jucys-Murphy sum, and the colour fibre is the tensor product of the column Specht modules $\bigotimes_jS^{\mu^{(j)}}$ by ordinary Schur-Weyl. Row permutations carry this fibre to every other colour fibre and span $e_SV(A)$, so dimension counting gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(A))\cong S(A)$, and by adjunction $\pi(N(A))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,N(A))\cong S(A)$.

Tilting images. A tilting object has a standard flag and a costandard flag by [F1]; applying the exact functor $\pi$ to the standard flag expresses $\pi$ of the tilting with the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag coefficients, and the standard/socle polarity used for full faithfulness on tiltings shows that the quotient is fully faithful there.

Outside the stable range. If $q_l<d$ the admissible-origin construction enlarges the pyramid by adding full ground rows until $d$ rows are distinct; contractible labels restrict to the original pyramid and the corner $e_S$ detects exactly them, so the identification of step 1.1 descends to the original objects; this is the same enlargement used for the central corner and it does not change the Hecke roots.

The simple images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ exactness of $\pi$ and the quotient description of [F2] give $\pi(L(A))=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))=D(A)$, and the cosocle of the Specht module $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ is $D(A)$ by the canonical highest-vector argument; since $\pi$ kills exactly the off-standard simples, $D(A)=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$, and the standard labels give all distinct simples of $B_d$ because every Hecke simple is a composition factor of some $S(A)$ and distinct standard labels give non-isomorphic $D(A)$.

Projective images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the cover $P(A)$ lies in $\operatorname{add}(T)$ by [F2]; hence $\pi(P(A))$ is a direct summand of $\pi(T)=B_d$, so it is projective, and its head is $D(A)$ by exactness, which makes it the projective cover $Y(A)$ of $D(A)$; the elementary identity $\pi^*\pi\cong\mathrm{id}$ on $\operatorname{add}(T)$ then gives $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$. For off-standard labels the image $\pi(P(A))$ is the genuine image of an ambient projective and is not claimed to be projective.

Multiplicities. Since $\pi$ is exact and its kernel is generated by the off-standard simples, the composition multiplicities of $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ are the multiplicities of the simple $L(B)$ in $N(A)$ for $B\in\mathrm{Std}$; by the Fock-space dictionary [F4] the typed coefficient of the dual-canonical/canonical pairing equals $d_{B,A}(1)$, so $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$; for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}$ the module $D(B)$ is zero and is not a simple Hecke label. All the identifications above are ungraded and taken at parameter $1$.

citations.quote: Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C)$ and let the standard parabolic $\mathfrak p$ have Levi $\mathfrak{gl}_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak{gl}_{n_l}$ ([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]).

Fix a finite genuine parabolic central summand: an integral block $\mathcal C$ of a parabolic category $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ ([[thm-parabolic-category-o-is-a-highest-weight-category]]) that is a **finite highest-weight block** with the following data.

Every label $A$ in a genuine tableau parabolic block of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]] has a unique indecomposable tilting object $T(A)$ whose standard flag begins with $M(A)$ once at the bottom and has all remaining labels $B<A$.

Keep the pyramid and admissible origins $c$ of [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], the ground object $P_c$, the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ and its central decomposition.

For admissible origins $c$ the genuine Whittaker functor $V$ of [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]] is exact on $\mathcal O_c^d$, and $$\gamma\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{W}(V_c^{\otimes d},V(-))$$ is a natural isomorphism, where $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$.

The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but not every projective.
Outside the stable range the central-corner identification uses the admissible-origin corner of [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].

Let $W_d=\varphi_d(W(\lambda))\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V_c^{\otimes d})$ be the image of the finite W-algebra and let $B_d=\psi_d(H_d(\Lambda))$ be the image of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] under the right action.

For nonadmissible $c$ the genuine image algebra and the full tensor double centralizer still exist by [[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]], but the same central-corner/Morita conclusion is not inferred without admissibility.

Transition duality gives $$\langle P_A,L_B\rangle=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde L_A,T_B)=\delta_{AB},\qquad C(\widetilde T_A,L_B)=\delta_{AB}.$$ All four families are Laurent-integral bases of the finite Fock cuts and commute with the upper-cut and common-bottom-tail embeddings.
Simples, projectives and tiltings therefore give the dual-canonical, quasi-canonical and canonical Fock families respectively.

The **degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is the quotient $$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$ the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial ([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]], [[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).
